questions.question: Which river originates from ‘Rakshastal north-western tip’ near Mansarovar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sutlej River**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sutlej River** originates from the north-western tip of Lake Rakshastal near Mansarovar in Tibet.
 
• The Sutlej River is one of the major rivers of the Indus basin and is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• It flows generally west and southwest through the Punjab region, forming part of the boundary between India and Pakistan before merging with the Chenab River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Sutlej River is also known as the Red River.
 
• It is an important source of irrigation and hydroelectric power in the region.
 
• The river has a significant cultural and historical importance, being mentioned in ancient Indian texts and associated with various historical events.
 
• It is part of the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan, which governs the use of the waters of the Indus River system.

questions.question: Which of the following options is NOT correctly matched?

questions.question:
Which of the following are salt-water lakes?

a. Sambhar lake

b. Dal lake

c. Wular lake

d. Chilika lake
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a and d**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sambhar lake** and **Chilika lake** are salt-water lakes.
 
• **Sambhar lake** is India's largest inland salt-water lake located in Rajasthan.
 
• **Chilika lake** is the largest coastal lagoon in India and the second largest in the world, situated in Odisha.
 
• **Dal lake** and **Wular lake** are freshwater lakes located in Jammu and Kashmir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dal lake** is known for its houseboats and scenic beauty, often referred to as the "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir".
 
• **Wular lake** is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, crucial for the hydrography of the Kashmir region.
 
• Salt-water lakes are usually found in regions with high evaporation rates and limited outflow, leading to the accumulation of salts.
 
• These lakes play a significant role in the local economy and ecology, supporting various species of flora and fauna.

questions.question: Identify the dam that is located in South India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mettur dam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mettur Dam** stands as one of **India's largest and Tamil Nadu's** foremost, situated at the point where the **Kaveri River **enters the plains.
 
• Constructed in 1934, its completion spanned nine years. With dimensions reaching a maximum height of 214 feet and width of 171 feet, the dam collects water from its own catchment area as well as the Kabini Dam and Krishna Raja Sagara Dams in Karnataka.
 
• Adjacent to the dam lies Ellis Park, overseen by the Tamil Nadu Public Works Department.
 
• Serving over 12 districts in Tamil Nadu with irrigation and drinking water, the dam is hailed as the vital source of life and sustenance for the region. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rihand Dam** (Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar) is the second-largest dam in India by storage volume and is located in Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• **The Gandhi Sagar Dam **is among the quartet of major dams erected along India's Chambal River, situated in the Mandsaur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• **Tilaiya Dam** marked the inaugural installment among the four multipurpose dams incorporated in the inaugural phase of the Damodar Valley Corporation. Positioned across the Barakar River, it stands at Tilaiya in the Koderma district of the Indian state of Jharkhand, inaugurated in 1953.

questions.question: Dihang and Lohit are rivers in which of the following regions?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh and Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmaputra River**

 
 
• **​The Brahmaputra, one of the largest rivers in the world**, has its origin in the **Chemayungdung glacier of the Kailash range near the Mansarovar lake**.

 
 
• From here, it traverses eastward longitudinally for a distance of nearly **1,200 km** in a dry and flat region of southern Tibet, where it is known as the **Tsangpo**, **which means 'the purifier'.**
 
• The Rango Tsangpo is the major right-bank tributary of this river in Tibet. It emerges as a turbulent and dynamic river after **carving out a deep gorge in the Central Himalayas near Namcha Barwa (7,755 m)**.
 
• The river emerges from the foothills under the name of **Siang or Dihang**.
 
 
 
• It enters India from **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
 
• Flowing southwest, it receives its main left-bank tributaries, viz., **Dibang or Sikang and Lohit,** thereafter, it is known as the **Brahmaputra.**
 
 
 
• The Brahmaputra receives numerous tributaries in its **750 km **long journey through the **Assam valley**.
 
 
• **Its major left bank tributaries are the Burhi Dihing and Dhansari (South) whereas the important right bank tributaries are the Subansiri, Kameng, Manas and Sankosh. The Subansiri which has its origin in Tibet**, is an antecedent river.
 
 
 
• The Brahmaputra enters Bangladesh near **Dhubri **and flows southward.
 
 
• **In Bangladesh, the Tista joins** it on its right bank from where the river is** known as the Jamuna**.
 
• It finally **merges with the river Padma,** which falls in the **Bay of Bengal.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of river lengths?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga, Godavari, Krishna, Yamuna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ganga: **

 
 
• **​**The length of the river Ganga is 2,525km.
 
• Ganga is a transboundary river of South Asia. It flows through India and Bangladesh.
 
• The river originates from the Gangotri glacier which is situated in the western Himalayas in Uttarakhand.
 
• The river flows south and east through the Gangetic plain of India and Bangladesh and finally emptied into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The left-bank tributaries are Gomti, Gandak, Ghaghra, Kosi, Ramganga and Mahananda and the right-bank tributaries include Yamuna, Son and Damodar, Tamsa and Punpun rivers.
 
 
 
• **Godavari:**
 
 
• **​**The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• Godavari river rises from Trimbakeshwar near Nasik in Maharashtra and flows for a length of about **1465 km** before outfalling into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjra, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner and the Sabri.
 
 
 
• **Krishna:**
 
 
• **The length of the Krishna River is 1400 km** and the coverage area is 258,948 square km.
 
• Krishna River is the fourth largest river in India after Ganga, Godavari, and Brahmaputra.
 
• It traces its course through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh states of India.
 
• The tributaries of the Krishna River are Bhima, Tungabhadra, Veena, Panchganga, etc.
 
• The Krishna river finally falls into the Bay of Bengal at Hamsaladeevi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The area of the drainage basin of the Krishna River is 258948 square km.
 
• Bhima, Dindi, Peddavagu, Musi, etc are the left bank tributaries of the Krishna River.
 
• Kudali, Venna, Koyna, Panchganga, etc are the right bank tributaries of the Krishna River.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna:**
 
 
• River Yamuna originates from Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand Himalayan Region.
 
• **The length of River Yamuna is around 1376 Km** and it merges with River Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad) Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The river Yamuna is the longest tributary of the river Ganga.
 
• River Yamuna flows through Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi.
 
• Some of the important cities in the bank of river Yamuna are Agra, Mathura, Delhi, Prayagraj (Allahabad).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f688b6475db419260362a92565c08925f5fa46206569f5165b7748c6e68c00ce.png]

questions.question: In which state of India is Tawa dam located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Tawa Reservoir is a reservoir on the **Tawa River in central India**. **It is located in Itarsi of Hoshangabad District of Madhya Pradesh state**, above Betul district.
 
• The reservoir was formed by the construction of the Tawa Dam, which began in 1958 and was** completed in 1978.**
 
• The dam** provides water for irrigation in Hoshangabad and Harda districts**.
 
• The Tawa reservoir forms the **western boundary of Satpura National Park and Bori Wildlife Sanctuary.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tawa Matsya Sangh** – a federation of Fisherworker’s cooperatives – an organization fighting for the rights of the displaced forest dwellers of the Satpura forest in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The newly formed Tawa Matsya Sangh (TMS) organized rallies and a chakka jam (road blockade), demanding their right to continue fishing for their livelihood.
 
• In response to their protests, the government created a committee to assess the issue.
 
• The committee recommended that fishing rights be granted to the villagers for their livelihood.
 
• **In 1996, the Madhya Pradesh government decided to give to the people displaced by the Tawa dam the fishing rights for the reservoir.**

questions.question: ________ are NOT considered surface water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aquifers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aquifers** are **underground layers** of **water-bearing rock**.
 
• They are **not considered surface water** because they are **beneath the Earth's surface**.
 
• **Surface water** refers to **bodies of water above the ground**, such as oceans, lakes, and rivers.
 
• **Aquifers** are a **crucial source of groundwater** but are **distinct** from **surface water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oceans**

 
 
• **Oceans** are **large bodies of saltwater** that cover the majority of the **Earth's surface**.
 
• They are considered **surface water** because they are** located** on the **Earth's exterior**.
 
• Oceans play a critical role in regulating the **planet's climate**, **weather patterns**, and **ecosystems**.
 
 
 
• **Lakes**
 
 
• **Lakes** are** large bodies** of** water** that are **surrounded by land**.
 
• They are considered **surface water **because they exist a**bove the Earth's surface**.
 
• Lakes can vary **greatly in size**, **depth,** and **characteristics**.
 
 
 
• **Rivers**
 
 
• **Rivers** are **natural watercourses **that flow from **higher to lower** **elevations**, usually towards the sea or another body of water.
 
• They are classified as **surface water** as they flow **above the Earth's surface**.
 
• Rivers play a crucial role in the **hydrological cycle**, **transporting water**, **sediment**, and **nutrients across landscapes**.

questions.question:
Choose the correct statement about the peninsular rivers.

a. The Narmada rises in the Malwa plateau.

b. The Godavari rises from the slopes of the Western Ghats near Nashik.

c. The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh.

d. The Krishna rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only b, c and d**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Only b, c, and d** are correct statements about the peninsular rivers of India.
 
• The Godavari rises from the slopes of the Western Ghats near Nashik.
 
• The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh.
 
• The Krishna rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar.
 
• The Narmada, however, does not rise in the Malwa plateau; it rises in the Amarkantak plateau.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The peninsular rivers of India are primarily rain-fed and have a seasonal flow pattern.
 
• These rivers flow through the Deccan Plateau and are characterized by their mature stage, having wider valleys and lower gradients.
 
• Major peninsular rivers include the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, and Mahanadi, which flow eastwards into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Narmada and Tapti are notable exceptions as they flow westwards into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: In which district of Uttarakhand does the Ramganga river originate from the Doodhatoli ranges?

__
 
• The Ramganga River originates from the **Namik Glacier, Doodhatoli ranges in the Pauri Garhwal **district of Uttarakhand.
 
• The river stretch is about 150 km before joining the Ganges.
 
• The Ramganga has several tributaries including the **Gori Ganga, Kosi, Aril, Khoh, and Deoha (Garra).**
 
• Ramganga **meets the Ganges at Kashipur**, Udham singh Nagar District of Uttarakhand. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The famous temples of Uttarakhand, **Baleshwar Temple, and Purnagiri Temple** are in the Champawat district.
 
• The** Nanda Devi Biosphere is located in Chamoli** district of Uttarakhand.
 
• The second highest peak of India Nanda Devi located in Chamoli.
 
• Famous **Badrinath temple, Valley of Flowers National Park, and Hemkund Sahib** are located in the Chamoli district.
 
• Kasaar Devi Temple**, Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, **Jageshwar temple located in Almora district of Uttarakhand.
 
• The **Chand dynasty** established Almora.
 
• The important rivers that play a vital role in Uttarakhand's agriculture are **The Ganges, Yamuna, Bhagirathi, Alaknanda, Kosi, Tons, and Pindar.**

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is joined by the Chambal River from the south?

__
 
• The Chambal River joins the Yamuna River from the south.
 
• Chambal is one of the major tributaries of the Yamuna River.
 
• The Chambal River originates in the Vindhya Range just south of Mhow in western Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows in a northerly direction through Madhya Pradesh before turning southeast to form the boundary between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and then between Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Eventually, it merges with the Yamuna River in Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Yamuna is the longest and the second-largest tributary river of the Ganges (Ganga) in northern India.
 
• It originates from the Yamunotri Glacier at a height of about 6,387 meters on the southwestern slopes of Banderpooch peaks in the Lower Himalayas in Uttarakhand.
 
• Yamuna traverses several states including Uttarakhand, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi.
 
• Key cities along the Yamuna include Delhi, Agra, and Mathura.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about River Ganga?

options.text: The water level of River Ganga never depends on monsoon and climatic condition of the Himalaya.
River Ganga and its river basin support lots of wonderful wildlife, particularly river dolphins, otters, freshwater turtles, and gharials.
River Ganga flows from the Himalayas all the way to the Bay of Bengal.
River Ganga in India is more than 2500 km long and is the most populated river basin in the world.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The water level of River Ganga never depends on monsoon and climatic condition of the Himalaya.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the water level of River Ganga does depend on monsoon and the climatic conditions of the Himalayas.
 
• **River Ganga** and its river basin support a diverse range of wildlife, including river dolphins, otters, freshwater turtles, and gharials.
 
• **River Ganga** flows from the Himalayas all the way to the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **River Ganga** in India is more than 2500 km long and is the most populated river basin in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ganga River is considered sacred in Hinduism and is worshipped as the goddess Ganga.
 
• The river is crucial for irrigation, drinking water, and transportation for millions of people living in its basin.
 
• Several initiatives have been launched to clean and protect the river, including the Namami Gange Programme by the Government of India.
 
• Despite its importance, the Ganga faces significant pollution challenges from industrial discharge, domestic sewage, and religious offerings.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of Ganga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bhima__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhima River:-

 
 
• Bhima River, a major tributary of the Krishna River, flows through Maharashtra and Karnataka states, western India.
 
• It rises in the Bhimashankar heights of the Western Ghats and flows southeastward for 450 miles (725 km) in Maharashtra to join the Krishna in Karnataka. **Major tributaries are the Sina and Nira rivers.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Krishna River:

 
 
• The Krishna is the second-largest east-flowing river of the Peninsula.
 
• The Krishna Basin extends over Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka having a total area of ~2.6 lakh Sq.km.
 
• It is bounded by the Balaghat range on the north, by the Eastern Ghats on the south and the east, and by the Western Ghats on the west.
 
• The Krishna River rises from the Western Ghats near Jor village of Satara district of Maharashtra at an altitude of 1,337 m just north of Mahabaleshwar.
 
• The total length of the river from its origin to its outfall into the Bay of Bengal is 1,400 km.
 
• The major part of the basin is covered with agricultural land accounting for 75.86% of the total area.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ganga is a transboundary river of Asia that flows through the nations of India and Bangladesh.
 
• The 2,525 km river rises in the western Himalayas in the Indian state of Uttarakhand and flows south and east through the Gangetic Plain of North India into Bangladesh, where it empties into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Ganga river system is the largest in India and has a number of perennial and non-perennial rivers originating in the Himalayas in the north and the Peninsula in the south, respectively.
 
• The Son is its major right-bank tributary.
 
• The important left-bank tributaries are the Ramganga, the Gomati, the Ghaghara, the Gandak, the Kosi, and the Mahananda.
 
• The river finally discharges itself into the Bay of Bengal near Sagar Island.
 
• The Yamuna, the westernmost and the longest tributary of the Ganga, has its source in the Yamunotri glacier on the western slopes of the Banderpunch range. It joins the Ganga at Prayag (Allahabad).

questions.question: What approximate percentage of geographical area of India is drained by river Godavari?

__
 
• The Godavari is the largest Peninsular river system. It is also called the Dakshin Ganga.
 
• Godavari river rises from Trimbakeshwar near Nasik in Maharashtra and flows for a length of about 1465 km before outfalling into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Union Territory of Puducherry.
 
• It drains approximately 10% of the geographical area of India.
 
• The basin is bounded by Satmala hills, the Ajanta range, and the Mahadeo hills on the north, by the Eastern Ghats on the south and the east and by the Western Ghats on the west.
 
• The left bank tributaries are more in number and larger in size than the right bank tributaries.
 
• Right Bank Tributaries: Shivna, Pravara, Mula, Sindphana, Manjra, Peddavagu, Maner.
 
• Left Bank Tributaries: Dharna, Penganga, Wainganga, Wardha, Pranahita [conveying the combined waters of Penganga, the Wardha and Wainganga], Pench, Kanhan, Sabari, Indravati.

questions.question: Which of the following river rise in the Nepal Himalaya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gandak:

 
 
• Gandak River, also called the Narayani River, river in central Nepal and northern India.
 
• It is formed by the union of the Kali and Trisuli rivers, which rise in the Great Himalaya Range in Nepal; from this junction to the Indian border the river is called the Narayani.
 
• It flows southwest into India and then turns southeast along with the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar state border and across the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
 
• It enters the Ganges (Ganga) River opposite Patna after a winding course of 475 miles (765 km).
 
• The Burhi (“Old”) Gandak flows parallel to and east of the Gandak River in an old channel.
 
• It joins the Ganges northeast of Munger.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chambal river:

 
 
• The Chambal is the chief tributary of the Yamuna River and rises in the Vindhya Range just south of Mhow, western Madhya Pradesh state.
 
• From its source, it flows north into the southeastern Rajasthan state. 
 
• Turning northeast, it flows past Kota and along the Rajasthan–Madhya Pradesh border; shifting east-southeast, it forms a portion of the **Uttar Pradesh-Madhya Pradesh border** and flows through Uttar Pradesh to empty into the Yamuna after a 550-mile (900-km) course.
 
• The Banas, Kali Sindh, Sipra, and Parbati are its chief tributaries.
 
 
 
• **Godavari is the largest peninsular river in India.**
 
 
• The second longest river in India after the Ganga.
 
• Originates from Triambakeshwar, Maharashtra.
 
• Flowing through Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh states.
 
• Also known as Vridha Ganga.
 
• Major left-bank tributaries: Purna, Pranhita, Indravati, and Sabari rivers.
 
• Major right bank tributaries: Pravara, Manjira, and Manair rivers.
 
• The Pranhita river is the largest tributary of Godavari.
 
• Important dams built across the Godavari river: Jayakwadi dam, Gangapur Dam, Babli project, and Sriram Sagar Dam.
 
• The Coringa mangrove forest is situated in the Godavari delta.
 
 
 
• Narmada River 
 
 
• Is the longest river of Madhya Pradesh, followed by the Tapti. 
 
• The Source of the Narmada is Narmada Kund which is located at Amarkantak in Anuppur District, Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada is also known as the Rewa.
 
• People from Madhya Pradesh depend fully on the Narmada River, they consider Narmada as the Life Line of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is one of the major rivers in India that run from east to west along with the Tapti and the Mahi.
 
• It flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh (1,077 km), Maharashtra (74 km), and in Gujarat (161 km).

questions.question: The drainage system formed when rivers discharge their waters from all directions in a lake or depression, as in the case of Loktak Lake in Manipur, is called ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **centripetal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Centripetal Drainage Pattern:**

__
 
• It is just the opposite of the radial as streams flow toward a central depression.
 
• During wetter portions of the year, these streams feed ephemeral lakes, which evaporate away during dry periods.
 
• Sometimes, salt flats are also created in these dry lake beds as salt dissolved in the lake water precipitates out of solution and is left behind when the water evaporates away.
 
• **E.g. Loktak lake in Manipur.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Radial Drainage Pattern:**

 
• The radial drainage pattern develops around a central elevated point and is common to conically shaped features such as volcanoes.
 
• When the rivers originate from a hill and flow in all directions, the drainage pattern is known as ‘radial’.
 
• E.g. The rivers originating from the** Amarkantak range; Narmada** and **Son (tributary of Ganga).**

**Trellis Drainage Pattern:**

 
• Trellis drainage develops in folded topography where hard and soft rocks exist parallel to each other.
 
• Down-turned folds called synclines form valleys in which reside the main channel of the stream.
 
• Such a pattern is formed when the primary tributaries of main rivers flow parallel to each other and secondary tributaries join them at right angles.
 
• **E.g. The rivers in the upper part of the Himalayan region; Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.**

**Dendritic Drainage Pattern:**

 
• It is the most common form and resembles the branching pattern of tree roots.
 
• The dendritic pattern develops where the river channel follows the slope of the terrain.
 
• The pattern develops in areas where the rock beneath the stream has no particular structure and can be eroded equally easily in all directions.
 
• Tributaries join larger streams at acute angles (less than 90°).
 
• **E.g. The rivers of the northern plains; Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/733ba9d541c73d179444da7d84d38741a60e28b6751039dc140626fe14c3488f.png]
